mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and begin to recover, commuting flows normalize and spill into discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both trend upward for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS relative to its recent level indicates reduced out-of-home leisure substitution, so fewer weekend outdoor trips leak away from shopping and RETAIL_REC improves over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20 and remains there for at least one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days after PARKS drops below -20, rejecting the claimed substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stays deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, mobility is being suppressed by restrictions or caution, which also depresses retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -20 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -20 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above 3 for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in GROCERY_PHARM usually reflects more routine local errands and normalized movement, which then supports nearby retail traffic and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above current levels for two or more weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rebounds from the prior week's trough while RETAIL_REC is still below baseline, outdoor activity and shopping trips are likely to co-move upward as weather-supported leisure broadens weekend travel.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points week-on-week after a week below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after PARKS rebounds by at least 8 points from a trough below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL from its elevated baseline signals fewer stay-at-home constraints, which should free trips into shopping districts and push RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3 after being at or above 3 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops below 3 from a higher prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES weakens while TRANSIT is already depressed, the commuting network is not feeding retail districts, so RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES falls and TRANSIT stays below -20 for most of the window.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a recovery in TRANSIT from its current low level should translate into more mall and street-level trips, producing a higher RETAIL_REC reading within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -25 after remaining below -25 for at least one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days after TRANSIT moves above -25 from a sustained sub -25 level.
